settings.prompt: Write a concise product spec for a cabin booking flow on MagicHouse, a premium nature-stay rental site. Cover: (1) entry point from the cabin hero/landing page, (2) date & guest selection in the booking panel, (3) review & guest details step, (4) payment step, (5) confirmation screen with itinerary and next steps. For each step describe: purpose, key UI elements, primary actions, validation rules, edge cases, and what data is persisted. Include a short user journey summary at the top and a list of states (loading, error, success) at the end. Keep tone product-focused, scannable, with clear headings.

Create a self-contained HTML mockup of Step 1 of the booking flow described in [#booking-flow-spec]: the cabin landing page with the booking panel. Show a premium hero photo of a desert dome cabin on the left, and a sticky glass-morphism booking panel on the right with: cabin name, location, star rating, price per night, date range picker (check-in / check-out), guest selector (adults / children), and a prominent 'Reserve' CTA. Use a warm, earthy palette (sand, terracotta, deep forest) with elegant serif headings and a modern sans for body. Include inline CSS only, no external assets — use CSS gradients/shapes for the cabin imagery. Make it look like a real product screen.

Create a self-contained HTML mockup of Step 2 of the booking flow described in [#booking-flow-spec]: the review & guest details page. Two-column layout — left: a guest details form (full name, email, phone, special requests textarea, checkbox for travel insurance); right: a sticky trip summary card showing cabin thumbnail, dates, number of nights, guest count, price breakdown (nightly rate × nights, cleaning fee, service fee, taxes, total). Include a stepper at the top (Dates → Details → Payment → Confirm) with step 2 active. Use the same warm earthy palette as step 1. Inline CSS only, no external assets. Add a 'Continue to payment' CTA at the bottom.

Create a self-contained HTML mockup of the final confirmation step of the booking flow described in [#booking-flow-spec]. Centered card layout with: a success checkmark/badge at top, headline 'Your stay is booked', booking reference code, cabin name + location, check-in/check-out dates with day-of-week, guest count, total paid, host contact card, and three next-step actions (Add to calendar, View itinerary, Message host). Below the card include a small section 'What to expect next' with 3 timeline items (confirmation email, check-in instructions 48h before, arrival). Use the same warm earthy palette and serif/sans pairing as previous steps. Inline CSS only, no external assets.

Create a self-contained HTML mockup — ALTERNATIVE A (Sub-stepper wizard) — for Step 2 of the booking flow described in [#booking-flow-spec], iterating on the baseline [#step-2-review-and-guest-details]. Pattern: SUB-STEPPER WIZARD with progressive disclosure. Break the form into 3 micro-steps inside step 2: (1) Guest info, (2) Add-ons (travel protection, early check-in, extras), (3) Payment summary preview. Show one micro-step at a time inside the left form card, with a slim progress bar at the top of the card and Back / Next pagination buttons at the bottom. The sticky trip summary card stays on the right (same content as the baseline: cabin thumbnail, dates, nights, guests, price breakdown, total). Keep the top stepper (Dates → Details → Payment → Confirm) with Details active. Reduces cognitive load and feels lighter, especially on mobile. Use the EXACT SAME MagicHouse warm earthy palette, glass-morphism, serif headings and sans body as the baseline step-2 mockup. Inline CSS only, no external assets. In the mockup, show micro-step 1 (Guest info) as the currently-active state with the progress bar 33% filled.

Create a self-contained HTML mockup — ALTERNATIVE B (Split-screen immersive) — for Step 2 of the booking flow described in [#booking-flow-spec], iterating on the baseline [#step-2-review-and-guest-details]. Pattern: SPLIT-SCREEN IMMERSIVE — edge-to-edge, no max-width container. Left 50% of the viewport: a full-bleed cinematic 'boarding pass' style photo of the desert dome cabin (use a rich CSS gradient/shape composition to evoke the desert dome at sunset). Overlaid at the bottom of the left half inside a dark gradient: cabin name, location, check-in / check-out dates, guest count and total price — feels like a travel boarding pass. Top-left over the image: minimal MagicHouse logo only. Right 50%: a scrollable single-column guest details form on a dark warm panel (full name, email, phone, special requests textarea, travel insurance checkbox, primary 'Confirm & pay' CTA at the bottom). Top-right over the form: a close ✕ button. Replace the heavy top stepper with a small 'Step 2 of 3 · Details' text label above the form heading. No separate summary card — booking context lives entirely in the photo half. Use the EXACT SAME MagicHouse warm earthy palette, serif headings and sans body as the baseline. Inline CSS only, no external assets.

Create a self-contained HTML mockup — ALTERNATIVE C (Sticky bottom action bar, mobile-first / app-like) — for Step 2 of the booking flow described in [#booking-flow-spec], iterating on the baseline [#step-2-review-and-guest-details]. Pattern: STICKY BOTTOM ACTION BAR with collapsible summary drawer. The guest details form takes the full content width as a single column (full name, email, phone, special requests, travel insurance) — NO side summary card. Keep the top stepper (Dates → Details → Payment → Confirm) with Details active. A persistent glass-morphism action bar is pinned to the bottom of the viewport showing on the left: a small cabin thumbnail + cabin name + total price, an expand chevron ▴; and on the right: a primary 'Confirm & pay →' button. Visualize the EXPANDED state of the drawer in the mockup — the drawer is open upward above the bar showing the full price breakdown (nightly rate × nights, cleaning fee, service fee, taxes, total) and the trip rows (check-in, check-out, guests) with a dashed perforated divider separating breakdown from the summary row. Works great on both mobile and desktop. Use the EXACT SAME MagicHouse warm earthy palette, glass-morphism, serif headings and sans body as the baseline. Inline CSS only, no external assets.

Open with exactly 2 sentences: what this canvas is for and what the user can do here. No intro, no extra text — just those 2 sentences. Display them in a large display font, left-aligned, white background.
